title: Identify your system and visible hardware
goal: Separate distribution, kernel, CPU and virtual device evidence.
challenge: Create a short inventory that identifies this guest distribution, running kernel, architecture, CPU count and one PCI device. Explain which observations describe the guest rather than all physical host devices.

steps.command: w=/home/learner/ll-discovery-1; test "$(id -un)" = learner && test ! -e "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && mkdir -m 0700 -- "$w" && cd -- "$w" && test "$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}')" -ge 65536
steps.explanation: Create a fresh private workspace; stop on collision or insufficient space.
steps.expected: Exact learner path, no existing entry, at least64MiB free.

steps.command: guard() { local links; test "$(pwd -P)" = /home/learner/ll-discovery-1 && test ! -L /home/learner/ll-discovery-1 && test "$(stat -c %U .)" = learner && links=$(sudo find . -type l -print -quit) && test -z "$links"; }; guard
steps.expected: No path substitution; guest root can override guest safeguards.

steps.command: unrelated() { dpkg-query -W -f='${binary:Package}\t${Version}\t${db:Status-Status}\n' | awk '$1!="ll-discovery-data" && $1!="ll-discovery-report"'; }; unrelated > before.tsv; sudo sha256sum /etc/sudoers.d/learning-lab > sudo.before; id learner > learner.before; scope_ok() { guard && unrelated > after.tsv && cmp before.tsv after.tsv && sudo sha256sum -c sudo.before && id learner > learner.after && cmp learner.before learner.after; }; scope_ok
steps.explanation: Retain unrelated package and learner/sudo evidence before any transaction.
steps.expected: Protected unrelated state captured; stop on mismatch.

steps.command: guard && { cat /etc/os-release; uname -r; uname -m; } > system.txt && cat system.txt
steps.explanation: Distribution and kernel versions are different facts.
steps.expected: Debian 13 and this running kernel/architecture; do not assume fixed host CPU text.

steps.command: guard && lscpu > cpu.txt && head -n 14 cpu.txt && lspci -nn > pci.txt && head -n 8 pci.txt
steps.explanation: PCI numeric IDs help identify devices. This guest has virtual hardware.
steps.expected: Two vCPUs and a virtual PCI inventory; no USB tool or physical-device configuration exercise.

steps.command: guard && { head -n 4 /proc/meminfo; ls /sys/bus/pci/devices | head -n 8; } > evidence.txt && cat evidence.txt
steps.explanation: /proc and /sys expose kernel observations, not ordinary saved files.

hints: uname -r reports the kernel, not Debian release.
Use the PCI numeric IDs alongside device descriptions.
A VM does not expose every physical host device.
review: Inventory with distribution, kernel, architecture, CPU count and a PCI ID; explain virtual hardware.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 101.1 partial hardware/resource discovery. Self-reviewed, unscored; not complete objectives.
